title: car-pi vehicle definition
description: Manufacturer-specific reads for one platform. Everything here is UDS ReadDataByIdentifier, which is read-only; there is no way to express a write in this schema, deliberately.

fictional.description: True for fixtures that describe a simulated vehicle rather than a real one. Such a profile is never matched against a real car.

match.description: How this profile is selected for a vehicle. Omit for a profile that is only ever chosen explicitly.

vin_prefix.description: Match if the vehicle's VIN starts with any of these. The World Manufacturer Identifier is the first three characters.

confidence.description: 'verified' requires confirmation against a real vehicle whose behaviour was independently known -- not merely that a plausible number came back.

request_id.description: Arbitration ID to send to. 11-bit unless `extended` is set.

session.description: Diagnostic session to request first. Programming sessions cannot be expressed; only these two are permitted.

safety_critical.description: Marks a module whose misconfiguration is dangerous -- airbag, ABS, steering, immobiliser. Reads are always safe, so this is advisory here; it exists so that any future write path has an unambiguous flag to refuse on.

id.description: Fact name. Reads sharing an id across ECUs are compared against each other -- which is how the cross-module odometer check works.

verified_on.description: Vehicles this read was actually confirmed against.

type.description: uint/int are big-endian; ascii and bcd are read as text and digits.

offset.description: Byte offset into the payload. Manufacturer identifiers frequently pack several values together.

add.description: Added after scaling, for encodings offset from zero.

range.description: Physically plausible [min, max]. A value outside it is reported as suspect rather than as fact, which matters a great deal for an unverified definition.
